title: Completed group algebra, augmentation ideal and canonical discrete action
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and $G$ a profinite group. For each open normal subgroup $U$ put $A_U=\Lambda[G/U]$, with transition maps induced by the quotient homomorphisms. Define $A=\Lambda[[G]]$ as the subalgebra of $\prod_U A_U$ consisting of the compatible families, with the subspace topology from the product of the discrete rings $A_U$. Define $\epsilon:A\to\Lambda$ by summing coefficients in the coordinate $U=G$, and $I=\ker\epsilon$ with its inherited left $A$-module structure and subspace topology. For $g\in G$, its basis vectors in the quotient coordinates form a compatible family $[g]\in A$; their augmentations are one, giving $[g]-1\in I$. For every discrete continuous $\Lambda$-linear $G$-module $M$ [def-exc-continuous-cohomology], the canonical completed action is the unique $\Lambda$-algebra homomorphism $\alpha_M:A\to\operatorname{End}_\Lambda(M)$ such that $\alpha_M([g])=\rho_M(g)$ and each orbit map $a\mapsto\alpha_M(a)m$ is continuous to discrete $M$. Equivalently, for $m$ in a finite $G$-stable submodule fixed by $U$, the action uses the $U$-coordinate of $a$ and the usual finite group-ring action.
